title: Development and validation of a multi-locus DNA metabarcoding method
author: Alfred J. Arulandhu

Examine the PCR thermocycler to ensure that the run has completed at the correct temperatures and that there is no error messages.

The pooled PCR products of samples S1 to S10 are purified using the QIAquick PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol QIAGEN (Annex 3). Ethanol is already added to the PE buffer, ready to use.

steps.title: Prepare samples for DNA isolation
steps.instruction: Weigh 100 ± 10 mg of each of the 11 samples (and the negative control) into separate 2 mL tubes.

steps.title: Add lysis reagents and vortex
steps.instruction: To each tube add 300 µL nuclease‑free molecular‑grade water, then 700 µL CTAB extraction buffer, vortex at maximum speed (~1000 rpm) for 10 seconds, add 5 µL RNase (100 mg/µL) and gently shake.

steps.title: Heat‑lysis and proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate tubes at 65 °C for 15 minutes in a Thermo‑Shaker at maximum speed (~1000 rpm), then add 20 µL proteinase K (20 mg/mL) solution and shake the tubes again.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at ~18 000 × g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: First chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 500 µL chloroform, transfer the supernatant from each sample into the chloroform tube, shake by hand for 30 seconds, then centrifuge at ~18 000 × g for 10 minutes until two clear phases form.

steps.title: Second chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper aqueous layer (~700 µL) to a new 1.5 mL tube, add an equal volume (≈700 µL) of chloroform, shake for 30 seconds, and centrifuge again at ~18 000 × g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper layer to a new 2 mL tube (≈500‑600 µL depending on the sample).

steps.title: CTAB precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 2 volumes of CTAB precipitation buffer (1200 µL) to each tube, mix by pipetting up and down, and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Pellet DNA and wash with NaCl/chloroform
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at ~18 000 × g for 10 minutes, discard supernatant, add 350 µL 1.2 M NaCl to the pellet, then add 350 µL chloroform, vortex for 30 seconds, and centrifuge again at ~18 000 × g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper layer to a new 1.5 mL tube, add 2 volumes ice‑cold 96 % ethanol (≈700 µL), gently invert several times, then store the tubes overnight at –20 °C.

steps.title: Ethanol wash and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: The next day centrifuge at ~18 000 × g for 30 minutes, discard supernatant, add 500 µL 70 % ethanol to wash the pellet, centrifuge 5 minutes at ~18 000 × g, remove all supernatant without displacing the pellet, add 100 µL nuclease‑free water, and let the pellet dissolve overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final DNA cleanup
steps.instruction: Vortex the dissolved DNA, short‑spin 10 seconds in a mini‑centrifuge, measure concentration with a NanoDrop ND1000 (negative control must show no DNA), dilute each sample to 10 ng/µL with nuclease‑free water to obtain 100 µL, label tubes and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mixes
steps.instruction: For each of the 12 barcode‑marker primer pairs, thaw primers, vortex and spin down, then assemble a PCR master mix in a 1.5 mL tube using the provided reagents and volumes (Table 1). Vortex the mix for 10 seconds and spin down 15 seconds in a mini‑centrifuge.

steps.title: Dispense PCR mix and add templates
steps.instruction: Aliquot 20 µL of each PCR master mix into the wells as indicated in Table 3, add 5 µL of sample DNA (10 ng/µL) to each well, add 5 µL of the appropriate positive‑control DNA (Bos taurus for animal markers, Lactuca sativa for plant markers), and add 5 µL ddH₂O for negative‑control wells.

steps.title: Run PCR program
steps.instruction: Place the PCR strip tubes in a thermocycler block with plastic caps, close the lid, and start the extended thermal profile as provided. After the run, spin down the strips for 15 seconds in a mini‑centrifuge and gently remove the caps.

steps.title: Check PCR products by gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load 5 µL of each sample, positive‑control and negative‑control reaction onto a 1 % agarose gel (or microchip system), run with an appropriate stain (e.g., ethidium bromide), compare bands to a 100 bp DNA ladder, and confirm that negative controls show no bands. Store PCR products at 4 °C until pooling.

steps.title: Pool PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: On a new day vortex all PCR tubes for 5 seconds and spin down 10 seconds in a micro‑centrifuge. For each sample (S1‑S10) transfer 8 µL from each of its 12 marker reactions into a single 1.5 mL tube (row A of Plate 1).

steps.title: Purify pooled amplicons
steps.instruction: Purify each pooled sample using QIAquick PCR purification columns, eluting with 30 µL of the supplied elution buffer.

steps.title: Quantify and adjust pooled DNA
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of each purified pool with a NanoDrop ND1000. If a pool is <15 ng/µL, repeat the QIAquick purification using a larger input volume (>10 µL of PCR mixture). Prepare an aliquot of at least 12.5 µL per sample with a concentration ≥15 ng/µL.

steps.title: Label and store final amplicons
steps.instruction: Label each aliquoted amplicon with sample name, date and laboratory number, and store at 4 °C.
